site.what: The markdown plugin is scanned as markup (EXTRA_MARKUP) and also as a reader, because it is a tools/src .ts file. So every hook it emits counts as read by itself. A dead or renamed hook in the diagram figure is never a finding in the markup. The spec's criterion is that renaming a hook in markup only gives two findings, one in the module and one in the markup. For this file it gives one.
site.evidence: Planted a dead hook: `'data-kb-diagram-stage': '', 'data-kb-plant-dead': ''` at tools/src/lib/site-markdown.ts:310. The gate exits 0: `[site-hooks] 14 behaviour modules and 29 markup files name the same hooks: 39 queried, 46 emitted, 1 kept for a reader` (46 emitted, up from 45, and no finding). Renamed `'data-kb-diagram-stage'` to `'data-kb-diagram-stadium'` in the same file only. The gate exits 1 with one finding, `[site-hooks] FAIL site/src/components/DiagramTools/diagram-tools.client.ts:20: data-kb-diagram-stage is queried here and no site markup emits it…`, and none for the unread data-kb-diagram-stadium. Spec kb.site.components Criteria: "Renaming a hook attribute in markup only gives exit 1 with two findings: one in the module, one in the markup."
site.fix: In the reverse pass, leave EXTRA_MARKUP files out of the text readers. Credit only the one handoff hook (data-kb-wide) as read there, for example through a named SELF_READ set, or through an entry in docs/data/allow/site-hooks.json. Add a check-site-hooks.test.ts case that renames a hook in the plugin and expects two findings.

site.what: The token gate reports an id selector, a URL fragment or an attribute-selector fragment as a colour whenever the name is exactly 3, 4, 6 or 8 hex letters. components-C2 says hex-like text that is not a colour, "such as an id selector or a URL fragment", is not a finding.
site.evidence: Appended to site/src/components/Lens/lens.css: `#ace .kb-plant-n4 { color: var(--sl-color-white); }`, `.kb-plant-n5 { mask: url(#fade); }` and `a[href="#cafe"].kb-plant-n6 {…}`. The gate exits 1 with `[site-tokens] FAIL site/src/components/Lens/lens.css:46: \`#ace\` is a colour literal…`, `…:47: \`#fade\` is a colour literal…` and `…:48: \`#cafe\` is a colour literal…`. In the same run, `#main-content …` and the comment `/* was #b4232a, rgb(1 2 3) */` correctly passed.
site.fix: Match a hex colour only in a declaration value: after a `:` inside a `{…}` block, and not inside `url(…)` or a quoted string. A simpler option is to blank selectors (the text before each `{`) and `url(...)`/string contents before scanning. Add the three near-misses to check-site-tokens.test.ts.

site.what: Named files can widen the scan, and misuse is not exit 2 (contract-C4: named files narrow a scan and never widen it; a named file the gate does not govern is misuse, exit 2). A non-.css name makes the gate walk the whole tree. A missing file is silently dropped with exit 0. A stylesheet outside site/src is read and judged. P1's check-json throws UsageError for a missing named file and never widens.
site.evidence: `tsx check-site-tokens.ts README.md` exits 0: `[site-tokens] 23 stylesheets under site/src take every colour from a token…`, the whole tree walked. `tsx check-site-tokens.ts site/src/nope.css` exits 0: `[site-tokens] 0 stylesheets under site/src…`. `tsx check-site-tokens.ts site/assets/pattern.css` exits 1: `[site-tokens] FAIL site/assets/pattern.css:163: \`#e0a800\` is a colour literal…`, a legacy file outside ROOT.
site.fix: Throw UsageError for a named path that does not exist, or that is a .css file outside site/src. Drop other names without falling back to the whole-tree walk. Walk the tree only when no argument was given, or when the only argument is the gate's own program (the driver's --changed case). Add a test for each case.

site.what: The portability gate finds a root-absolute reference only in the double-quoted form `href="/…"`. A single-quoted or unquoted one passes. site-links reads either quote style but resolves a leading `/` from the page's own folder. On the home page, a single-quoted root-absolute link passes all three built-site gates, although it opens nothing from file:// (offline-C3: no built page carries an href or src starting with a single `/`).
site.evidence: In circuit-breaker.html, site-portable reported only line 3192 (`href="/patterns.html"`) and missed line 3193 `` and line 3194 ``. site-links named them with a wrong base: `link '/patterns.html' → patterns/distributed/resilience/patterns.html does not exist`. With `` planted in site/dist/index.html's article, all three gates exit 0: `check-site-portable exit 0`, `check-site-links exit 0`, `check-site-absence exit 0`.

In check-site-links, treat a leading `/` as a finding, or resolve it from the site root, not from `${dir}/`.

site.what: The payload anchor check is a substring test, `html.includes(`id="${h.id}"`)`. It also matches `data-id="…"` (every mermaid edge carries one), so a search heading whose anchor exists only as a data-id passes. offline-C6: only heading ids present in their page.

site.what: Finding paths are built from the raw `--dist` string. With an absolute --dist, a real finding turns into an exit-2 crash from the framework's path check, with the gate name printed twice and the finding lost. With `--dist ./site/dist/`, paths come out as `./site/dist//…`, which is not a normalised root-relative path (contract-C5). site-absence and site-links normalise with path.relative; site-portable does not.
site.evidence: With `tabindex="3"` planted: `tsx check-site-portable.ts --dist /private/tmp/kb-site-oracle/site/dist` gives `abs exit 2 out=0` and stderr `[site-portable] [site-portable] finding path "/private/tmp/kb-site-oracle/site/dist/patterns/distributed/resilience/circuit-breaker.html" is not root-relative without spaces`. `--dist ./site/dist/` prints `[site-portable] FAIL ./site/dist//patterns/distributed/resilience/circuit-breaker.html:3192: positive tabindex…`.
site.fix: Compute `shown` as `path.relative(ctx.root, abs)` (posix separators), as check-site-links does, and use it for every finding path. Add a test with an absolute and a trailing-slash --dist.

site.what: build-command-O1's order proof reads `${stdout}${stderr}` joined end to end, not the real interleaving. The site-gate lines (stderr) come after every stdout marker by construction, so 'then the site-gate lines' after post-build can never fail on order.

The prebuild step's `[gen-map-pages] note: no area …` lines appear after `[gen-search-index] 3 pages…` from postbuild. The test comment says "the order is the proof".
site.fix: Run make with the two streams merged at the source, for example `spawnSync('sh', ['-c', 'make --no-print-directory site-build 2>&1'])`, or stdio pointing both at one pipe. Then the marker and gate-line order is what happened.

site.what: The canonical link, og:url and sitemap URLs leave out the project path the site is served under. README.md says the site is live at https://odere-pro.github.io/patterns-kb/, but every built page names https://odere-pro.github.io/patterns/…. Starlight builds the canonical as new URL(pathname, site), so setting SITE_URL to a URL with a path cannot fix it. After the cutover deploy, every page's canonical, its og:url and the sitemap would point at URLs that do not exist. No gate sees this, because site-links skips external URLs.

README.md:7 reads 'Live at **https://odere-pro.github.io/patterns-kb/**.'

site.what: components-C2 is not met: an id selector and a URL fragment that happen to look like a hex colour are reported as colours. It also misses a colour function written in upper case (components-C1). The rule tells a colour from other text by digit count alone, and it matches function names case-sensitively.

The gate reported `[site-tokens] FAIL site/src/components/Lens/lens.css:43: `#fade` is a colour literal` and `…lens.css:44: `#abcdef` is a colour literal`, and said nothing about line 49 (HSL). Regex: /#(?:[0-9a-fA-F]{8}|[0-9a-fA-F]{6}|[0-9a-fA-F]{4}|[0-9a-fA-F]{3})\b|\b(?:rgba?|hsla?)\s*\(/g.
site.fix: Skip `#hex` in selector position (before a `{` block, outside declarations) and inside `url(…)`. Match rgb/rgba/hsl/hsla in any case. Add a test case for each.

kbcli.where: tools/src/kb/rank.ts proseLines (lines 242-271): every block goes into the prose index, including the generated relationships, tour and fluency regions
kbcli.what: find and brief score a page against its neighbours' titles. In v1 the relationship row's Title text ran together into one word ('Gopuffinventory'), so a one-word title was never indexed. In v2 each row '- [Gopuff](…) — note' indexes the title whole. So a query for a design or pattern name returns every page related to it, pushes real hits out of the top eight, and changes brief's governing theme. No DECIDED entry covers it. The deviation 'only the lower part of a ranking can reorder' does not describe it.
kbcli.evidence: find gopuff --json: v1 = [gopuff] (1 hit); v2 = gopuff,cache-aside,in-process-cache,stateless-service,sharding,replication,geohash,scatter-gather. v2's `why` for cache-aside is 'Gopuff — inventory is read from cache first, populated on miss…', which is the relationships row at docs/patterns/caching/cache-aside.md:241. v1's source is site/patterns/caching/cache-aside.html:459 `Gopuffinventory is read…`. find chatgpt: v1 1 hit, v2 8. find uber: v1 6, v2 8. find youtube: v1 youtube,top-k,video-recommendations,sharding; v2 youtube,sharding,top-k,pipe-filter,cdn,… (top five share 3; video-recommendations falls to rank 10). brief --json governing theme: youtube video-recommendations → system-design-interview; gopuff null → system-design-interview; chatgpt null → workload-composition; sweeper long-running-tasks → operating-a-live-system, because v2's hits self-healing and robinhood come in. Across all 1,037 page-name and alias queries, run in-process through both scorers: top hit the same on all; hit count differs on 73 (pattern 40, design 18, comparison 12); top five share fewer than 4 on 39 (e.g. 'prototype' v1 4 hits, v2 7: abstract-factory, factory-method, builder). That breaks the rule parity.test.ts holds find to ('same top hit, share at least 4 of the top five, same number of hits'). The rule only passes because its 13 queries are symptoms. v1 kept `.mentions` out of its index for this reason ('indexing it would score a page against words it never wrote').
kbcli.fix: Decide it explicitly. Option (a): index only the note of generated rows, not the link text. I tried dropping link text in generated regions in my worktree: the design-name differences went away, but others moved (v1 indexed every word of a title except the last, e.g. 'minimize coordination' then shared only 2 of the top five), so re-measure relevance.test.ts and parity afterwards. Option (b): add a DECIDED entry that names the behaviour, and add page-name queries (find gopuff, brief youtube) to the parity set with the rule they are held to.

kbcli.evidence: Sandbox with docs/patterns/gof/creational made read-only: `kb.mjs link circuit-breaker combines-with singleton --note x` printed "kb.mjs: Error: EACCES: permission denied, open '…/singleton.md.tmp.86758'". Afterwards relations.json and circuit-breaker.md differed from the base, and singleton.md was unchanged.
kbcli.fix: Write every temp file first, then rename them all. Or, on a failed write, put back the files already replaced. Test it with an unwritable folder.

kbcli.what: `set` refuses a CRLF page and blames a well-formed key. The one parser reads the same page fine (frontmatter-C10: CRLF reads the same as LF).
kbcli.evidence: After converting circuit-breaker.md to CRLF, fm-json.sh printed {"title": "Circuit Breaker", "description": "Stops calling a service that's already failing"}. `kb.mjs set circuit-breaker --favourite false` then printed "…: the frontmatter holds a line that is not one `key: value` (\"title: Circuit Breaker\")", exit 1. The shape regex is tested against lines split on '\n' only, so the trailing '\r' fails it. splitFrontmatter also needs line 1 to be exactly `---`, while lib-frontmatter.sh:117 accepts `^---[[:space:]]*$`.
kbcli.fix: Split on /\r?\n/ in fmShapeProblem and keep the page's line ending when writing it back. Accept trailing whitespace on the opening fence the way the parser does. Add a CRLF case to edit.test.ts.
